sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r8/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 10 / #9; Internal Quality Checks row 10 / #9)
evidence: Frozen task.toml [environment] (lines 20-24): build_timeout_sec=600.0, network_mode="public", cpus=2, memory_mb=4096; no docker_image key, no allow_internet key, and no secret literal under [environment]. Lines 17-38 are byte-identical to the frozen template task.toml (diff of everything after line 16 is empty); the only credential is the template ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} placeholder under [verifier.env] (row 10's scope, intentional per SKILL.md line 66). environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template Dockerfile (node:22-bookworm-slim, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 installed globally with NODE_PATH, no ENV/ARG secrets). 2 CPUs/4 GiB is ample for a single Node/Express/better-sqlite3 app (prebuilt binaries, no native compile needed at grade time). Nothing secretly needs an install: solution package.json depends only on express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1 (exact preinstalled versions), server.js requires only those plus node built-ins, solve.sh only copies files, and integration.md line 3 tells the agent both are preinstalled via NODE_PATH. Grep of environment/ for api_key/secret/token/password finds only the intentional demo password 'password123' (walls-and-retention.md line 3); seed emails are fictitious @kittle.test. The Internal Quality Checks annotation says 'no-network', but the public workbook row, SKILL.md line 26 and quality-checks.md say public network is correct, so it is not flagged. Raw-evidence-index records the agent image built and the golden installed via the frozen solve.sh (package.json 242a3215..., solve.sh f7c17a01..., seed b256f85e..., server.js e4d9402d... all match current frozen bytes, verified with sha256sum). Probes: a broken app that runs npm install at start would still fail only at runtime if network were absent, but network is public in both phases so it is not a posture defect; a conforming app using only the preinstalled modules runs within the declared resources. I did not build the image myself in this review.
